speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin my evaluation, on which side of your neck is the pain located, and does it radiate to a specific area in your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with bilateral Upper Limb Radiculopathy.

The patient's presentation of chronic burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness over the past year, combined with his history of diabetes and a prior motor vehicle accident, is highly suggestive of cervical spine degeneration and myelopathy. Given the progressive nature and bilateral symptoms, I need to confirm the structural findings. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
